oil.summary: WTI surged 2.55% to $84.14/bbl, driven squarely by a Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery — the kingdom's largest — with Saudi air defenses reportedly intercepting drones over the facility. Separately, two tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, compounding supply-route anxiety as the Iran war continues to reshape global crude flows; Iran also reported three additional tankers hitting mines in Hormuz. Despite the geopolitical premium, Brent slipped 0.69% to $90.77, RBOB fell 1.43%, and heating oil dropped 1.65%, suggesting product markets remain pressured by the month-long demand-side selloff (Brent -20.3% on the month). U.S. crude inventories rose 1.1 million barrels last week, adding a mild bearish offset. The WTI/Brent spread divergence is notable. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC+ cut at the May 2026 meeting.
drivers: Houthi drone strike on Ras Tanura refinery and tanker explosions/mines in the Strait of Hormuz spike supply-disruption premium in WTI
Iran war accelerating shift of fuel tankers into crude trade; Russia becomes top supplier to India and China as Iranian barrels are disrupted
Bearish offset from rising U.S. crude inventories (+1.1 mb) and sharp month-long product price declines; OPEC+ cut odds at 77% for May

gas.summary: Henry Hub rocketed 10.59% to $3.676/MMBtu, extending a sharp monthly rally of over 36%, with the Iran war and broader Middle East supply disruption cited as the primary driver lifting global energy complex sentiment. UK household energy bills are reported set to soar 26% from the start of next year, directly linked to Iran-war-driven gas price pressure. TTF pulled back 3.89% to €88.1/MWh on the day despite holding an 8.97% weekly gain, suggesting some profit-taking after last week's run-up. European gas policy signals remain deeply contradictory: the EU is advancing legislation to ban Russian gas imports while U.S. envoys are simultaneously pitching a plan to resume Russian gas flows via Ukraine. The U.S. rig count held flat this week even as domestic oil production hit a fifth consecutive record.
drivers: Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruptions driving broad energy risk premium, lifting Henry Hub +10.6% on the day and +36% on the month
Contradictory European policy signals: EU advancing Russian gas ban while U.S. envoys propose resuming Russian gas flows to Europe via Ukraine
UK energy bills set to rise 26% as Iran-war gas price shock feeds through to consumer tariffs; U.S. rig count flat despite record oil output

power.summary: EU carbon (EUA) edged down 0.97% to $78.26/EUA, trimming a modest weekly gain of 2.63% but remaining 6.6% below last month's levels. TTF's 3.89% daily retreat provides some relief to gas-fired power generation margins in Europe, though the weekly and monthly context keeps the power stack under pressure. Iran's electricity rationing under U.S. sanctions and blockade highlights how deeply the conflict is affecting domestic energy infrastructure beyond crude exports. On the structural side, a headline flagged real momentum building for small modular reactors in the U.S., and Big Oil and Big Tech are jointly lobbying the EU for faster permitting of gas-fired data centers. The EU's 22nd Russia sanctions package is in motion, with questions raised about whether Brussels' sanctions machinery is approaching its operational limits.
drivers: EUA softens slightly as TTF pulls back on the day, but monthly carbon weakness reflects broader demand uncertainty and energy cost pressure in Europe
Iran electricity rationing under sanctions illustrates conflict's systemic power-sector spillover beyond crude markets
SMR momentum building in the U.S.; Big Oil and Big Tech lobbying EU for expedited gas-fired data center permits signals rising power-demand expectations
